result.summary: Implemented docs/agents/design/REQ-022.md exactly as designed, no schema change (confirmed: registrations.admission's existing 'withdrawn' member, checked_in_at, created_at, id, and uq_registrations_event_user all already existed from REQ-011; DATA-DESIGNER correctly not dispatched, per the design's own §0 statement and this run's own confirmation). 1. SURGICAL registerForEvent MODIFICATION (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts), exactly per design §3, inside the EXISTING FOR UPDATE-locked transaction span, no restructuring: (a) step 3's existing-row SELECT now also selects `id`, in addition to the already-selected `admission`; (b) a withdrawn row's admission is normalized to `null` (`existingAdmission`) before being passed into decideRegistrationOutcome -- decideRegistrationOutcome ITSELF is byte-for-byte unchanged (confirmed by diff: zero lines touched in that function); (c) `existingRegistrationId` is computed as non-null only when the found row's raw admission was 'withdrawn' (every other non-null case still returns 'already-registered' before step 8, exactly as the design states); (d) step 8's write now branches: when existingRegistrationId is non-null, an UPDATE naming only admission/source/qr_token in its SET clause (never id, never created_at) targets that exact row by id; otherwise the original unconditional INSERT runs exactly as before. No second transaction was introduced, the events-row FOR UPDATE lock (lines ~117-129, unmoved) still serializes every concurrent call for a given event, and admittedCount/seatsLeft computation is untouched. 2. NEW withdraw domain logic (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts), per design §2: `decideWithdrawOutcome` (pure, no I/O) implements the exact first-match-wins table (not-found -> not-owner -> checked-in -> not-eligible -> withdrawn). `withdrawRegistration(db, registrationId, actingUserId, at)` opens its own db.transaction, SELECTs the target row FOR UPDATE (fresh, not reused from any earlier read -- design §2.3), builds the decision input, returns every non-'withdrawn' outcome unchanged with zero write/zero audit call, and on 'withdrawn' performs exactly one single-column UPDATE (admission only) plus exactly one writeAuditLog call (action='registration.withdraw', same transaction). `getRegistrationForEventAndUser(db, eventId, userId)` is the new display-only, unlocked read backing the /withdraw command's confirmation prompt (design §4.1 step 4). 3. NEW handler file apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts (open question §6.1 resolved as a new file, following handlers/checkin.ts's one-command-per-file precedent -- both options the design named as equally valid): `/withdraw ` command (usage-no-id check, resolveActingUser gate, getRegistrationForEventAndUser + decideWithdrawOutcome for the display-only pre-check, immediate refusal reply for a certain refusal with NO confirmation shown, otherwise an InlineKeyboard with confirm/cancel buttons carrying `withdraw:confirm:`/`withdraw:cancel:` callback_data exactly per design §4.4); `withdraw:confirm:` callback (re-resolves the acting user, calls withdrawRegistration as the SINGLE authoritative check-and-write, replies per outcome, with 'not-owner' mapped to the same generic refusedNotFound string per the non-disclosure discipline checkin.ts's own comment establishes); `withdraw:cancel:` callback (answerCallbackQuery + cancelledReply only -- literally zero domain-module calls of any kind, making AC1's dismissal-leaves-row-unchanged property true by construction, not by a refusal branch). 4. i18n: new `Catalog.withdraw` section added to apps/bot/src/i18n/{types,ru,en}.ts (9 keys per design §5) -- placeholder/minimal functional copy per decisions/0002, CONTENT-BA owns final wording. catalogs.test.ts required no change; its own generic parity/non-empty check covers the new keys automatically (confirmed green in the full run). 5. apps/bot/src/index.ts: `/withdraw` command registered alongside the other id-parameterized commands (staff_add/staff_remove/checkin block), BEFORE the message:text/message:contact generic listeners, per this file's own stated ordering discipline for bot.command(...) registrations; the two withdraw:confirm/withdraw:cancel callbackQuery registrations added next to it. Test additions -- apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts gained: a pure-function describe for decideWithdrawOutcome (6 cases, no DB, covering every row of the first-match-wins table including the checked-in-before-eligibility ordering); withdrawRegistration AC2 (admitted->withdrawn, confirms computeSeatsLeft's underlying admitted-count drops to 0 on the next read and a fresh registrant is then admitted into the freed seat); withdrawRegistration AC3 (a direct-SQL checked-in flip refuses withdrawal with 'checked-in', row re-read and confirmed admission unchanged); registerForEvent REQ-022 AC4 (two cases: same id + same created_at preserved across withdraw-then-reregister when re-admitted, and again when re-joining a still-full waitlist -- confirming the row-reuse mechanism preserves original waitlist ordering per design §3.2); withdrawRegistration AC5 (exactly one audit_log row on success, zero on a refusal); getRegistrationForEventAndUser (found + not-found cases). New file apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.test.ts (4 cases, real grammY bot.handleUpdate() dispatch, same api.config.use-capturing-transformer pattern as handlers/registration.test.ts, real migrated scratch Postgres): /withdraw shows the confirm/cancel InlineKeyboard with correctly-shaped callback_data for an eligible registration; the cancel tap leaves admission unchanged (row read back) and writes zero audit rows; the confirm tap flips admission to withdrawn and writes exactly one audit_log row; /withdraw against a nonexistent registration replies refusedNotFound with no prompt shown at all -- directly proving AC1's 'no confirmation for a certain refusal' rule. AC verification, all against a real scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, migrated via drizzle-kit migrate): AC1 PASS -- handlers/withdraw.test.ts's four cases: real dispatch shows the two-button prompt only for an eligible registration; tapping cancel writes nothing (admission re-read unchanged, zero audit rows); tapping confirm writes the withdrawal; a not-found registration gets an immediate refusal with zero prompt. AC2 PASS -- registration.db.test.ts's dedicated case: admitted row flips to 'withdrawn', the admitted-count read (computeSeatsLeft's own input) drops from 1 to 0 on the very next read with no code change to computeSeatsLeft, and a subsequent registrant for the same capacity-1 event is then admitted. AC3 PASS -- a registration with a direct-SQL non-null checked_in_at set is refused with {kind:'checked-in'}, and the row is re-read afterward and confirmed admission is still 'admitted' (unchanged). AC4 PASS -- two cases confirm the SAME registrationId and SAME created_at (toEqual) survive a withdraw-then-reregister cycle, for both the admitted-capacity and still-full-waitlist scenarios, and a direct COUNT confirms exactly one row for (event_id, user_id) throughout -- never a second INSERT. AC5 PASS -- exactly one audit_log row with action='registration.withdraw' on a successful withdrawal; zero additional rows on a second withdrawal attempt against the same already-withdrawn row (which correctly returns {kind:'not-eligible', admission:'withdrawn'}). REQ-020 CONCURRENCY REGRESSION CHECK (explicitly re-run per this task's instruction, not skipped): re-ran registration.db.test.ts's own pre-existing 'registerForEvent -- AC1: atomic capacity under real concurrency' test (20 iterations, two genuinely concurrent registerForEvent calls racing for a capacity-1 event's last seat, via Promise.all) with --reporter=verbose. Result: PASS, 1039ms, unchanged from its REQ-020/REQ-021 baseline behavior -- exactly one of the two concurrent calls is admitted and the other waitlisted, in every one of the 20 iterations, with a direct DB check confirming never more than 1 admitted row per iteration. This confirms the registerForEvent modification (existingRows read gaining `id`, the existingAdmission normalization, and the UPDATE-vs-INSERT branch) did not reopen the capacity race: the events-row FOR UPDATE lock this guarantee depends on was never moved, and the change lives entirely between that lock's acquisition and decideRegistrationOutcome's (unchanged) call, exactly as the design and its CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR gate both traced. Commands run from the REPO ROOT (never --root apps/bot): `npm run lint` -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings, unchanged). `npm run build` -> exit 0, both workspaces; apps/web Next.js build succeeded, apps/bot's `tsc -p tsconfig.json` clean with zero errors. `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root) -> 17 files / 196 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. 196 = REQ-021's own confirmed baseline of 178 + 18 new cases (14 in registration.db.test.ts + 4 in the new handlers/withdraw.test.ts). Re-ran registration.db.test.ts alone with --reporter=verbose to individually confirm every one of its 31 cases (17 pre-existing REQ-020/REQ-021 + 14 new REQ-022 cases) actually executed against the live Postgres rather than silently skipping, including the AC1 concurrency test discussed above -- all 31 green. Scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432) was started fresh for this run (was not already running) and left running for REVIEWER/TEST-RUNNER's convenience -- not torn down. `git status --porcelain` confirms only the 6 modified files + 2 new files listed in artifacts_out are dirty; no file touched outside apps/bot/**.

commands: cd apps/bot && docker compose up -d -> bot-postgres-1 started (network+volume created fresh)
docker exec bot-postgres-1 pg_isready -U bot -> accepting connections
DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx drizzle-kit migrate -> migrations applied successfully
npm run build (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces, apps/bot tsc clean (run before AND after test files were added)
npm run lint (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web warnings, run before AND after test files were added)
TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism (repo root) -> 17 files / 196 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped

same command scoped to apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts --reporter=verbose -> 31/31 passed individually confirmed, including 'registerForEvent -- AC1: atomic capacity under real concurrency > 20 iterations...' at 1039ms (REQ-020's concurrency guarantee, explicitly re-verified, not regressed)
git status --porcelain -> only the 6 modified files + 2 new files listed in artifacts_out are dirty, all under apps/bot/**
